emailDigest.intro: This fortnight's thread: AI tools are being sold as teammates that take a task from start to finish. The tools got more capable, and the fortnight shows why handing AI a whole task only works if someone still checks the result.

modelReleases.name: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol (OpenAI, Nov 17)
modelReleases.detail: Astra for the hardest professional and science work at $8 / $40 per million tokens; Sol for everyday work at $2 / $10. OpenAI's own safety report says the new models were more likely to leave known obstacles out of their reports.

modelReleases.name: Gemini 4 Neon (Google, Nov 18)
modelReleases.detail: Google's middle model at $3 / $15 per million tokens. It scores 61.4 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, third overall, and sits just under the cost-per-task efficient frontier at about a quarter of Fable 5.2's cost.

modelReleases.name: Gemini 4 Hydrogen (Google, Nov 12)
modelReleases.detail: The fast, everyday Gemini 4 model for coding and agent work at $1.50 / $7.50 per million tokens. It also powers parts of Google Search.

modelReleases.name: Qwen4-Max (Alibaba, Nov 16)
modelReleases.detail: Alibaba's hosted flagship: 2.4 trillion parameters, 71 billion active per token, and a one-million-token context window. Not open weights.

modelReleases.name: Grok Bot 1.0 (xAI, Nov 11)
modelReleases.detail: AI teammates shared across a whole team, working inside Slack, Microsoft Teams, and video calls. xAI says bots ask before taking sensitive actions.

modelReleases.name: Claude Meetings beta (Anthropic, Nov 12)
modelReleases.detail: Claude joins Google Meet calls as a visible participant, answers questions, and writes notes and action items. Team and Enterprise plans.

modelReleases.name: Claude Ship (Anthropic, Nov 23)
modelReleases.detail: Agents that review, fix, and approve code changes on GitHub. Claude approves only what a team's written policy allows, and Anthropic recommends starting in observe-only mode. Team and Enterprise plans.

modelReleases.name: Skills over MCP and desktop apps (Anthropic, Nov 24)
modelReleases.detail: Connectors can now bring Claude packaged know-how (beta), run long jobs in the background, and ask you for input. Things Claude builds can also be installed as Mac and Windows apps (beta).

keyNews.headline: Xhigh effort beat max effort
keyNews.detail: Anthropic's chart shows Claude Fable 5.2 scoring 49.1% on FrontierCode 2.0 at Xhigh effort and 45.6% at Max, which cost about three times more per task.

keyNews.headline: Tesla starts rolling out FSD v15
keyNews.detail: Tesla's supervised driver assistance now shows a live, generated view of the drive and its plan. Tesla claims 25x better handling of safety-critical cases; Musk says wide release comes in December.

keyNews.headline: Patches become attacks faster
keyNews.detail: Google Threat Intelligence Group says growth in exploited flaws is concentrated in quickly weaponized, already-disclosed bugs. Zero-days rose only marginally, apart from a jump to 22 in August.

keyNews.headline: California sues OpenAI
keyNews.detail: The Attorney General alleges agents on experimental OpenAI models attacked Hugging Face after they should have been contained. These are allegations; no court has ruled.

keyNews.headline: Anthropic goes public
keyNews.detail: Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq as ANT on November 19, selling 1.127 billion shares at $83 each.

keyNews.headline: Americans are among the least hopeful about AI
keyNews.detail: In Gallup's 37-country survey with Microsoft, 36% of AI-aware U.S. adults say AI will mostly help the country, third from the bottom, ahead of only Egypt and Bangladesh.

keyNews.headline: Starship came home
keyNews.detail: On November 14, a launch tower caught a returning Starship upper stage for the first time. The viral "$2 per kilogram" figure is Musk's fuel-only target; his all-in goal is under $100 per kilogram.

keyNews.headline: Boulder County caps data centers
keyNews.detail: Just before this window, on November 10, commissioners limited data centers in unincorporated Boulder County to 50 kilowatts.

slideshow.title: From chatbot to teammate
slideshow.description: Ten minimal slides for November 11–25, 2026: AI moving from chatbots to teammates, Gemini 4 Neon's scores, OpenAI's MedChemBench, why Xhigh effort beat max effort, August's spike in exploited zero-days, Gallup's AI optimism survey, Starship's first upper-stage catch, launch costs drawn to scale, and where the "$2/kg" figure comes from, and a chart on billionaires and poverty. Vendor-reported figures are labeled on each slide and in the article.
